To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a spatial data infrastructure (SDI) is an appropriate framework for organizing distributed sources of brain images, (2) the spatial SDI framework can be extended by adding distributed grid services, and (3) the SDI can be used to create a federated atlas environment for brain data visualization and spatial analysis.

the spatial data infrastructure (SDI) and Smart Atlas tools enable integration of heterogeneous brain images and markup from multiple distributed sources into a single atlas environment for online discovery, access, visualization and analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

development of a federated spatial data infrastructure (SDI) for brain data, which will enable researchers to discover, access and analyze heterogeneous images and markup from different brain projects.

the development of spatial data infrastructure and tools that will allow researchers and educators to discover, access and analyze brain data from multiple sources in a single federated spatial environment.
developing a spatial data infrastructure (SDI) for brain data and an atlas environment that will enable the integration of brain images and image markup from multiple sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain atlas has been developed and is available for use.
the spatial database and the Smart Atlas environment provide a powerful and flexible framework for integrating and analyzing distributed brain data.
this paper describes strategies and technologies to enable the discovery, visualization, and analysis of heterogeneous brain images and data from multiple sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are building a federated brain atlas environment that enables researchers to discover, access and analyze brain images from different projects and species, and to create a unified picture of brain morphology, function and pathology.

the integration of spatial data sources and atlas environment enables the discovery of heterogeneous brain data sources and the analysis of their spatial relationships, and thus, provides a framework for collaborative brain research.

we have demonstrated that a distributed atlas environment can be built using Web-enabled spatial data infrastructures and that the Smart Atlas provides a flexible and powerful framework for federated analysis and visualization of brain data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to integrate heterogeneous sources of brain images and markup into a single atlas environment.
the integration of distributed brain data is a feasible and important goal that requires the adoption of standards for spatial and semantic data representation and exchange.
the integration of heterogeneous spatial brain data is possible, and that it can be achieved through the use of open standards and open source software.
